approved: Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas (Import Levy) Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and introduces measures to prevent price exploitation and false representations about the repeal's effect on prices.

The amendments prohibit price exploitation for key goods like electricity and gas, with penalties of up to 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070) for corporations and 1,295 penalty units ($220,150) for individuals.

Electricity and natural gas retailers and bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers must provide substantiation statements to the ACCC explaining how cost savings from the repeal are passed on to customers.
Introduces a new prohibition on carbon-specific price exploitation for certain key goods.
Requires the ACCC to issue carbon tax removal substantiation notices to retailers and importers.
Requires retailers and importers to provide carbon tax removal substantiation statements to the ACCC.
Requires electricity and natural gas retailers to prepare and communicate statements to customers about cost savings.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the repeal on prices.
Introduces a prohibition on false or misleading representations about the repeal's effect on prices.
Electricity and natural gas retailers, bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers, and their customers.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track passage of the carbon tax repeal bills through the House together, arguing the September 2013 election gave the coalition a clear mandate, and recalled the 2010 pledge that there would be no carbon tax under a government Julia Gillard led.

Moved the second reading of the carbon tax repeal bills, saying Treasury modelling shows households will save an average of $550 a year, that the tax has cost $15 billion over two years, and citing an Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission estimate that electricity prices in the ACT will fall by 11.6 per cent once it is repealed.
